clauses.reason: Enacting words: the President acts under the Constitution and laws and orders what follows. The lead carries no command of its own and ends with section 1. First end of section 1: 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

Section 1 revokes the two listed orders, items (a) and (b). The order states no effective date, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, January 21, 2025; that is a reading of the heading and signature block, not express wording, and the alternative dates are the filing date (January 30, 2025) and the printing date (January 31, 2025). The revocation is a one-time act; once made it had nothing further to command. Quoted words: "The following Executive Orders are hereby revoked:". Actor: the order itself; no later act was needed. The surviving consequence, that the target order stays revoked, is recorded under savings.

This item of section 1 revokes Executive Order 14042 of September 9, 2021 (Ensuring Adequate COVID Safety Protocols for Federal Contractors). It is part of the one-time revocation in section 1: the order states no effective date, so it is read as taking effect on signing, 2025-01-21 (a reading of the heading and signature block, not express wording). Once made it had nothing further to command.

This item of section 1 revokes Executive Order 14043 of September 9, 2021 (Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees). It is part of the one-time revocation in section 1: the order states no effective date, so it is read as taking effect on signing, 2025-01-21 (a reading of the heading and signature block, not express wording). Once made it had nothing further to command.

This general provision says nothing in the order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the matters in its items (i) and (ii); it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

Item (i) of the non-derogation provision preserves the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

Item (ii) of the non-derogation provision preserves the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

This general provision says the order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations; it conditions how the order is carried out. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

This general provision states that the order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit enforceable at law or in equity against the United States or others; it states the order's effect. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-01-21 (signing on January 21, 2025).

The surviving consequence is that Executive Order 14042 of September 9, 2021 (Ensuring Adequate COVID Safety Protocols for Federal Contractors) and Executive Order 14043 of September 9, 2021 (Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees) stays revoked, which is an accrued effect of the completed act and not a continuing command of this order; the held sources show no open claim.
